questions.stem: A parent of a healthy 5-month-old who is exclusively breastfed asks whether the infant should start drinking water and eating cereal now because the weather is warm. Which response best reflects WHO guidance?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Begin small amounts of water now and postpone complementary foods until 9 months, while continuing breastfeeding whenever the infant appears hungry.","B":"Add small amounts of water between feeds during warm weather but continue avoiding solid foods until the infant has reached about 8 months of age.","C":"Begin cereal and pureed foods now because complementary feeding should start during the fifth month while breast milk remains the main nutrition source.","D":"Continue exclusive breastfeeding through about 6 months without routine water, then introduce safe complementary foods while breastfeeding continues."}}
questions.rationale: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months, meaning no other food or liquids including water, followed by safe complementary foods from about 6 months while breastfeeding continues to 2 years or beyond.
questions.source_detail: WHO and UNICEF recommend exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months, complementary foods from 6 months, and continued breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond.

questions.stem: An 18-month-old presents for a routine health-supervision visit. The parent has no specific developmental concerns. Which screening plan best reflects current AAP recommendations?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue developmental surveillance and perform both a standardized general developmental screen and an autism-specific screen during this 18-month visit.","B":"Perform developmental surveillance only because standardized developmental testing is reserved for children whose caregivers or clinicians report a concern.","C":"Perform an autism-specific screen but defer the general developmental screen until 24 months because both tools should not be used at the same visit.","D":"Perform a general developmental screen but defer autism screening until school age unless language regression or repetitive behavior is already present."}}
questions.rationale: AAP recommends developmental surveillance at every health-supervision visit, standardized general developmental screening at 9, 18, and 30 months, and autism-specific screening at 18 and 24 months. An 18-month visit therefore includes both standardized screens.
questions.source_name: American Academy of Pediatrics — Developmental Surveillance and Screening
questions.source_detail: AAP current patient-care guidance specifies developmental surveillance at every visit, general developmental screening at 9/18/30 months, and autism screening at 18/24 months.

questions.stem: A client who smokes daily says, “I know it is hurting my health, but I am not ready to quit.” Which nursing response best supports a productive behavior-change conversation?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"“You need to choose a quit date today because continuing to smoke after acknowledging the risk means education has already failed.”","B":"“I will avoid discussing smoking until you decide independently that you are ready to stop, because questions may increase resistance.”","C":"“What do you like about smoking, and what concerns you about it? We can talk about what you might want to change when you are ready.”","D":"“Since you understand the health effects, I will document refusal of cessation treatment and move on to the rest of the visit.”"}}
questions.rationale: A nonjudgmental, open-ended conversation can explore ambivalence without forcing action. SAMHSA recommends listening without judgment, asking open-ended questions, and supporting the person's own readiness for change.
questions.source_name: SAMHSA — How to Talk to Someone About Help for Mental Health & Substance Use
questions.source_detail: SAMHSA recommends open-ended questions, supportive language, reflective listening, and avoiding judgment when discussing substance use or behavior change.
